claim: Classical studies of attention have identified areas of parietal and frontal cortex as sources of attentional control.
source: Classical studies of attention have identified areas of parietal and frontal cortex as sources of attentional control.
evidence: This claim is supported by references to established scientific literature on attention networks.

claim: PITd, a ventral region in the macaque temporal cortex, has been suggested as a third attentional control area.
source: Recently, a ventral region in the macaque temporal cortex, the posterior infero-temporal dorsal area PITd, has been suggested as a third attentional control area.
evidence: This claim references recent findings about PITd's role in attention.

claim: PITd and dorsal attention areas are all directly connected through three specific fascicles.
source: By combining functional MRI with ex-vivo high-resolution diffusion MRI, we found that PITd and dorsal attention areas are all directly connected through three specific fascicles.
evidence: This claim is supported by the experimental data from combined fMRI and dMRI studies presented in the manuscript.

claim: The control of endogenous attention in macaque is exerted by a dorso-ventral network.
source: These results ascribe a new function, the communication of attention signals, to two known fiber-bundles, highlight the importance of vertical interactions across the two visual streams, and imply that the control of endogenous attention, hitherto thought to reside in macaque dorsal cortical areas, is exerted by a dorso-ventral network.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the connectivity data showing direct connections between dorsal and ventral attention areas.

claim: Endogenous attention is thought to be controlled by a fronto-parietal network.
source: Endogenous attention is thought to be controlled by a fronto-parietal network (Corbetta et al., 2008; Kastner and Ungerleider, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research on attention networks.

claim: The lateral intraparietal area (LIP) and the frontal eye field (FEF) exhibit key properties of attentional control.
source: In the macaque monkey brain, the lateral intraparietal area (LIP; Bisley and Goldberg, 2010; Gottlieb et al., 1998) and the frontal eye field (FEF; Thompson and Bichot, 2005) exhibit key properties of attentional control and are thought to form the core of the endogenous attention network (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research on LIP and FEF.

claim: PITd was even more strongly attention-modulated than LIP.
source: One of these studies (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016), found that an area in the lower bank of the Superior Temporal Sulcus (STS), the dorsal posterior infero-temporal area, PITd (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991; Saleem and Logothetis, 2007) was even more strongly attention-modulated than LIP, was engaged by multiple attention tasks, and was not modulated by the task-relevant feature dimension.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous fMRI study.

claim: PITd was engaged by multiple attention tasks.
source: One of these studies (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016), found that an area in the lower bank of the Superior Temporal Sulcus (STS), the dorsal posterior infero-temporal area, PITd (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991; Saleem and Logothetis, 2007) was even more strongly attention-modulated than LIP, was engaged by multiple attention tasks, and was not modulated by the task-relevant feature dimension.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous fMRI study.

claim: PITd was not modulated by the task-relevant feature dimension.
source: One of these studies (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016), found that an area in the lower bank of the Superior Temporal Sulcus (STS), the dorsal posterior infero-temporal area, PITd (Felleman and Van Essen, 1991; Saleem and Logothetis, 2007) was even more strongly attention-modulated than LIP, was engaged by multiple attention tasks, and was not modulated by the task-relevant feature dimension.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous fMRI study.

claim: PITd exhibits key properties of an attentional control area.
source: Thus PITd was shown to exhibit key properties of an attentional control area (Figure 1A–B; Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work and reference to figures showing functional properties.

claim: The human ventral attention network is functionally different from macaque area PITd.
source: A ventral attention network has been previously proposed in humans (Corbetta et al., 2008; Geng and Vossel, 2013). However, its functional properties are profoundly different from those of macaque area PITd.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations and comparison of functional properties.

claim: Human dorsal and ventral attention networks have different functional profiles, with the first primarily supporting endogenous attention, and the latter primarily supporting exogenous attention.
source: First, human dorsal and ventral attention networks have a different functional profile, with the first primarily supporting endogenous attention, and the latter primarily supporting exogenous attention (Corbetta et al., 2008), along with context updating (Geng and Vossel, 2013) and social cognition (Carter and Huettel, 2013; Mars et al., 2013; Schwiedrzik et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to human attention research.

claim: Ventral area PITd shared similar functional properties with dorsal areas LIP and FEF.
source: On the contrary ventral area PITd shared similar functional properties with dorsal areas LIP and FEF (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous functional study.

claim: The human temporo-parietal-junction (TPJ) is suppressed during endogenous attention.
source: Second, the most prominent part of the human ventral attention network, the temporo-parietal-junction (TPJ), is suppressed during endogenous attention, and activated during target detection and shifts of attention, particularly when stimuli are salient or unexpected (Corbetta et al., 2008; Corbetta and Shulman, 2002), whereas PITd was strongly activated during prolonged sustained attention (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to human attention research.

claim: PITd was strongly activated during prolonged sustained attention.
source: Second, the most prominent part of the human ventral attention network, the temporo-parietal-junction (TPJ), is suppressed during endogenous attention, and activated during target detection and shifts of attention, particularly when stimuli are salient or unexpected (Corbetta et al., 2008; Corbetta and Shulman, 2002), whereas PITd was strongly activated during prolonged sustained attention (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous functional study.

claim: Macaque PITd possesses a putative human homolog, phPITd, located far ventrally to TPJ.
source: Third, macaque PITd possesses a putative human homolog, phPITd, an area located far ventrally to TPJ (Glasser et al., 2016; Kolster et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to studies on cross-species homology.

claim: Long-range inter-areal connectivity is supported by the white matter.
source: Long-range inter-areal connectivity is supported by the white matter.
evidence: This is established knowledge in neuroscience.

claim: Fascicles respond to behavior by adapting density, shape, and molecular composition in a manner that corresponds to individual abilities in health and disease.
source: First, fascicles respond to behavior by adapting density, shape, and molecular composition in a manner that corresponds to individual abilities in health and disease (Fields, 2008; Jbabdi et al., 2015; Pestilli, 2018; Rokem et al., 2017; Thomason and Thompson, 2011; Wandell, 2016), and thus take an active role in shaping network function.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to research on white matter plasticity.

claim: The visual system is organized into two major posterior-anterior information-processing streams: a dorsal path for spatial processing, and a ventral path for feature and object processing.
source: The main organizing principle of the visual system is its separation into two major posterior-anterior information-processing streams: a dorsal path for spatial processing, and a ventral path for feature and object processing (Kravitz et al., 2013; Milner and Goodale, 1995).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to foundational work on visual stream organization.

claim: Previous anatomical studies have demonstrated strong and direct connections between parietal area LIP and frontal area FEF mainly via the Superior Longitudinal Fasciculus (SLF).
source: Previous anatomical studies have demonstrated strong and direct connections between parietal area LIP and frontal area FEF (Blatt et al., 1990; Lewis and Van Essen, 2000; Petrides and Pandya, 2006) mainly via the Superior Longitudinal Fasciculus (SLF).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies.

claim: Only a single classical anatomical study has targeted PITd.
source: More specifically, to date only a single classical anatomical study has targeted PITd (Distler et al., 1993), but due to the study's paucity of data and lack of functional characterization, the relationship to attention networks remains unclear.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation and assessment of the literature.

claim: A major superior-inferior diffusion direction exists in the lateral temporal white matter close to PITd.
source: Crucially, we found a major superior-inferior diffusion direction (blue) in the lateral temporal white matter close to PITd (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by diffusion MRI data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The superior-inferior diffusion direction in lateral temporal white matter is compatible with a direct vertical connection between PITd and LIP.
source: This is compatible with a direct vertical connection between PITd and LIP.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the diffusion direction data.

claim: A white matter tract connects PITd and LIP.
source: We found a white matter tract connecting the two areas (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The core of the PITd-LIP tract was observed at a consistent position for all subjects and hemispheres.
source: We observed the core of the tract at a consistent position for all subjects and hemispheres (Figure 3—figure supplement 1, yellow streamlines), thus validating the hypothesis of a direct vertical connection (Figure 1D, dark and light pink dashed lines).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data across multiple subjects.

claim: A white matter tract directly connects PITd and FEF.
source: We performed probabilistic tractography between PITd and FEF and successfully identified a white matter tract directly connecting PITd and FEF (Figure 3C).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The core of the PITd-FEF tract was observed for all subjects and hemispheres.
source: We observed the core of the tract for all subjects and hemispheres (Figure 3—figure supplement 1; cyan streamlines).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data across multiple subjects.

claim: LIP-PITd connections comprised an estimated 777 ± 300 streamlines across subjects.
source: Across subjects, LIP-PITd connections comprised an estimated 777 ± 300 streamlines and PITd-FEF connections 188.5 ± 77.8 streamlines.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative tractography measurements.

claim: PITd-FEF connections comprised an estimated 188.5 ± 77.8 streamlines across subjects.
source: Across subjects, LIP-PITd connections comprised an estimated 777 ± 300 streamlines and PITd-FEF connections 188.5 ± 77.8 streamlines.
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative tractography measurements.

claim: The fronto-temporal tract (PITd-FEF) was on average longer than the temporo-parietal connection (PITd-LIP).
source: The fronto-temporal tract was on average longer than the temporo-parietal connection (Figure 3D, left panel), it had a lower density and similar volume (Figure 3D, middle panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The PITd-FEF tract had a lower density than the PITd-LIP tract.
source: The fronto-temporal tract was on average longer than the temporo-parietal connection (Figure 3D, left panel), it had a lower density and similar volume (Figure 3D, middle panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The PITd-FEF tract had similar volume to the PITd-LIP tract.
source: The fronto-temporal tract was on average longer than the temporo-parietal connection (Figure 3D, left panel), it had a lower density and similar volume (Figure 3D, middle panels).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The strength of evidence values demonstrate statistically that the measured data has signal consistent with the reported tracts.
source: The strength of evidence values demonstrate statistically that the measured data has signal consistent with the reported tracts (Figure 3D, right panel).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis using LiFE method shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Direct LIP-FEF connections run through a component of the Superior Longitudinal Fasciculus (SLF).
source: First, we tested whether the connections between functionally defined areas LIP and FEF conform to the previously established finding, that direct LIP-FEF connections run through a component of the Superior Longitudinal Fasciculus (SLF; Figure 1D dark and light blue dashed lines; Blatt et al., 1990; Lewis and Van Essen, 2000; Petrides and Pandya, 2006), a notion obtained without specifically targeting attentional areas.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous anatomical studies and confirmed by current tractography data.

claim: Probabilistic tractography between FEF and LIP demonstrated a direct pathway between these two dorsal attention areas.
source: Probabilistic tractography between FEF and LIP demonstrated a direct pathway between these two dorsal attention areas (Figure 4A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1; orange).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The FEF-LIP connection had an average length comparable to the PITd-FEF tract but showed higher density and volume.
source: This fronto-parietal connection had an average length comparable to the PITd-FEF tract but showed higher density and volume (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: The FEF-LIP tract is part of the most dorso-medial region of SLFIII and the most ventro-medial region of SLFII.
source: The FEF-LIP tract is part of the most dorso-medial region of SLFIII and the most ventro-medial region of SLFII (Figure 4B, orange traces) thus lying at the intersection between SLFIII and SLFII and overlapping almost equally with both tracts (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical comparison shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: LIP-PITd tract is located anterior to VOF.
source: LIP-PITd tract is located anterior to VOF, runs mainly vertically, but it is also elongated from posterior to anterior (Figure 4F, yellow streamlines) and it almost completely overlap with the vILF (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by anatomical comparison shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The PITd-LIP tract almost completely overlaps with the vILF.
source: LIP-PITd tract is located anterior to VOF, runs mainly vertically, but it is also elongated from posterior to anterior (Figure 4F, yellow streamlines) and it almost completely overlap with the vILF (Figure 4G).
evidence: This claim is supported by quantitative overlap analysis shown in Figure 4G.

claim: No streamlines of the PITd-LIP tract run through the VOF.
source: We did not find any streamline running through the VOF (Figure 4E), and the only overlap between this tract and PITd-LIP connection occurs at the level of VOF termination in the temporal lobe (Figure 4F–G).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data shown in Figure 4E-G.

claim: PITd showed the highest degree of overlap with vILF among nearby areas.
source: Interestingly, when we functionally parceled areas nearby PITd to test for some degree of specificity in the way PITd connects to LIP, we found that PITd showed the highest degree of overlap with vILF (Figure 4—figure supplement 4A–C).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparative analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 4.

claim: The vILF contains a bundle connecting the two functionally defined attention areas PITd and LIP.
source: Here we show that the vILF also contains a bundle connecting the two functionally defined attention areas PITd and LIP, and provide anatomical and functional evidence for the proposed distinction between VOF and vILF (Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data and comparison with previous literature.

claim: FEF-PITd tract departs from the ILF and joins the EmC.
source: ILF continues anteriorly within the temporal lobe up to the anterior end of the lateral geniculate nucleus, whereas FEF-PITd tract defined through functional ROI tracking departs from the ILF (Figure 4I, cyan streamlines) and joins the EmC (Figure 4I, dark green streamlines).
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: No streamlines of the PITd-FEF tract run through the AF.
source: We did not find any streamline running through the AF (Figure 4I–L, light green), and the only overlap between this tract and PITd-FEF connection occurs at the level of the termination in the frontal lobe.
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data shown in Figure 4I-L.

claim: Attention-modulated area PITd connects to the FEF through the ILF and the EmC, rather than through the AF.
source: Thus, here we show that attention-modulated area PITd connects to the FEF through the ILF and the EmC, rather than through the AF.
evidence: This claim is supported by tractography data comparing different pathways.

claim: The vILF, but not the VOF, connects attention-modulated PITd with LIP.
source: Collectively, these results thus establish that the vILF, but not the VOF, connects attention-modulated PITd with LIP, and that the EmC, but not the AF, connects PITd to FEF.
evidence: This claim is supported by comprehensive tractography data comparing alternative pathways.

claim: The EmC, but not the AF, connects PITd to FEF.
source: Collectively, these results thus establish that the vILF, but not the VOF, connects attention-modulated PITd with LIP, and that the EmC, but not the AF, connects PITd to FEF.
evidence: This claim is supported by comprehensive tractography data comparing alternative pathways.

claim: Classical attentional control areas LIP and FEF are connected to PITd.
source: Here we show that, in the macaque brain, classical attentional control areas LIP, in posterior parietal cortex, and FEF, in prefrontal cortex, are connected to PITd, an area in temporal cortex only recently implied in endogenous attention (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by the tractography data presented in the study.

claim: PITd might be an endogenous attention control area.
source: We thus provide new evidence that PITd might be an endogenous attention control area, that attentional control may not be limited to dorsal fronto-parietal structures in the macaque brain, and that these areas form an attention network through direct connections (Figure 5 and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the connectivity data and functional properties of PITd.

claim: Attentional control may not be limited to dorsal fronto-parietal structures in the macaque brain.
source: We thus provide new evidence that PITd might be an endogenous attention control area, that attentional control may not be limited to dorsal fronto-parietal structures in the macaque brain, and that these areas form an attention network through direct connections (Figure 5 and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the discovery of PITd as an attention area with direct connections to dorsal areas.

claim: PITd, LIP, and FEF form an attention network through direct connections.
source: We thus provide new evidence that PITd might be an endogenous attention control area, that attentional control may not be limited to dorsal fronto-parietal structures in the macaque brain, and that these areas form an attention network through direct connections (Figure 5 and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by the tractography data showing direct connections between all three areas.

claim: PITd is a visual area located in the lower bank of the STS.
source: PITd is a visual area located in the lower bank of the STS, it contains neurons that are shape- and color-selective (Conway and Tsao, 2009; Hikosaka, 1998) and have circumscribed receptive fields slightly larger than those of V4 (Hikosaka, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous anatomical and physiological studies.

claim: PITd contains neurons that are shape- and color-selective.
source: PITd is a visual area located in the lower bank of the STS, it contains neurons that are shape- and color-selective (Conway and Tsao, 2009; Hikosaka, 1998) and have circumscribed receptive fields slightly larger than those of V4 (Hikosaka, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous physiological studies.

claim: PITd neurons have circumscribed receptive fields slightly larger than those of V4.
source: PITd is a visual area located in the lower bank of the STS, it contains neurons that are shape- and color-selective (Conway and Tsao, 2009; Hikosaka, 1998) and have circumscribed receptive fields slightly larger than those of V4 (Hikosaka, 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous physiological study.

claim: Functional specificity of PITd does not arise as a simple consequence of its connectivity with LIP and FEF.
source: Thus, functional specificity of PITd does not arise as a simple consequence of its connectivity with LIP and FEF.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that nearby areas share similar connectivity but differ functionally.

claim: PITd's connectivity scheme is different from the nearby face-processing network.
source: It is noteworthy that this connectivity scheme is different from the nearby face-processing network (Grimaldi et al., 2016; Moeller et al., 2008), which encompasses two face areas right next to attention-modulated area PITd (Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on face-processing networks.

claim: PITd's position within the ventral visual pathway is likely crucial to collect attention-relevant information about properties of objects.
source: In particular, PITd's position within the ventral visual pathway is likely crucial to collect attention-relevant information about properties of objects (Conway and Tsao, 2009; Hikosaka, 1998), including faces (Tsao et al., 2006) and gaze (Marciniak et al., 2014), possibly providing information on object value (Ghazizadeh et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on PITd's anatomical position and citations to related studies.

claim: Through the described connections, PITd might make important contributions to core functionality of endogenous attention and to a wide range of attention-related functions.
source: Through the described connections, PITd might thus make important contributions to core functionality of endogenous attention and to a wide range of attention-related functions.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the connectivity data.

claim: Macaque PITd bears neither functional nor structural similarity to human TPJ.
source: PITd thus bears neither functional nor structural similarity to human TPJ.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the comparison of functional properties and connectivity patterns.

claim: Human phPITd occupies a similar position in retinotopic cortex as macaque PITd.
source: Human phPITd occupies a similar positions in retinotopic cortex as macaque PITd, and, like PITd, is sensitive to two-dimensional shapes and is insensitive to motion (Kolster et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous comparative study.

claim: Human phPITd is sensitive to two-dimensional shapes and is insensitive to motion.
source: Human phPITd occupies a similar positions in retinotopic cortex as macaque PITd, and, like PITd, is sensitive to two-dimensional shapes and is insensitive to motion (Kolster et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Under a homology argument of attention network organization, human phPITd is predicted as the ventral node of the human endogenous attention network.
source: Our results predict, under a homology argument of attention network organization, this area as the ventral node of the human endogenous attention network.
evidence: This claim is a prediction based on cross-species comparison and homology reasoning.

claim: The properties of specific fiber-bundles have been found to correlate with attentive behaviors.
source: For example, the properties of specific fiber-bundles have been found to correlate with attentive behaviors (Chechlacz et al., 2015; Chica et al., 2018; Parlatini et al., 2017), and their disconnection results in attentional deficits like spatial neglect (Carter et al., 2017; Lunven and Bartolomeo, 2017), it is therefore of great importance to characterize their structure and path.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies on white matter and attention.

claim: Disconnection of specific fiber-bundles results in attentional deficits like spatial neglect.
source: For example, the properties of specific fiber-bundles have been found to correlate with attentive behaviors (Chechlacz et al., 2015; Chica et al., 2018; Parlatini et al., 2017), and their disconnection results in attentional deficits like spatial neglect (Carter et al., 2017; Lunven and Bartolomeo, 2017), it is therefore of great importance to characterize their structure and path.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous clinical studies.

claim: The vertical branch of the ILF, but not the VOF, connects the two posterior attention areas PITd with LIP.
source: We established that the vertical branch of the ILF, but not the VOF, connects the two posterior attention areas PITd with LIP, and that the ILF and the EmC, but not the AF, connects PITd to the dorsal prefrontal area FEF.
evidence: This claim is supported by comprehensive tractography data.

claim: The ILF and the EmC, but not the AF, connect PITd to the dorsal prefrontal area FEF.
source: We established that the vertical branch of the ILF, but not the VOF, connects the two posterior attention areas PITd with LIP, and that the ILF and the EmC, but not the AF, connects PITd to the dorsal prefrontal area FEF.
evidence: This claim is supported by comprehensive tractography data.

claim: The results imply a role in attentional control for the vILF and the ILF/EmC.
source: Our results thus imply a role in attentional control for the vILF and the ILF/EmC. (Figure 5 and Figure 5—video 1).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the finding that these fascicles connect attention areas.

claim: In humans, two distinct vertical fiber bundles that connect the dorsal and ventral visual streams have been described, the VOF and the posterior Arcuate Fasciculus (pAF).
source: In humans, two distinct vertical fiber bundles that connect the dorsal and ventral visual streams have been described, the VOF and the posterior Arcuate Fasciculus (pAF).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge from human neuroimaging literature.

claim: The VOF supports a variety of perceptual functions, like skilled reading and spatial orienting.
source: The VOF supports a variety of perceptual functions, like skilled reading and spatial orienting (Takemura et al., 2016b; Yeatman et al., 2014; Yeatman et al., 2013), the pAF, located anterior to the VOF (Catani and Thiebaut de Schotten, 2008; Thiebaut de Schotten et al., 2014; Weiner et al., 2017), is thought to support language (Catani and Thiebaut de Schotten, 2008; Thiebaut de Schotten et al., 2014) and action-to-object coordination (Budisavljevic et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous human neuroimaging studies.

claim: The human pAF is thought to support language and action-to-object coordination.
source: The VOF supports a variety of perceptual functions, like skilled reading and spatial orienting (Takemura et al., 2016b; Yeatman et al., 2014; Yeatman et al., 2013), the pAF, located anterior to the VOF (Catani and Thiebaut de Schotten, 2008; Thiebaut de Schotten et al., 2014; Weiner et al., 2017), is thought to support language (Catani and Thiebaut de Schotten, 2008; Thiebaut de Schotten et al., 2014) and action-to-object coordination (Budisavljevic et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous human neuroimaging studies.

claim: Human pAF may be a candidate tract for the exchange of attentional information between dorsal and ventral attention areas in the posterior part of the human brain.
source: Because of its anatomical location, its cortical endpoints, and its separation from the VOF, human pAF may be a candidate tract for the exchange of attentional information between dorsal and ventral attention areas in the posterior part of the human brain, thus being functionally and anatomically similar to the vILF.
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on anatomical comparison between human and macaque.

claim: Human EmC is important for language.
source: Human EmC is important for language (Catani and Bambini, 2014; Friederici and Gierhan, 2013) and may also carry attentional information (Umarova et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous human neuroimaging studies.

claim: Human EmC may carry attentional information.
source: Human EmC is important for language (Catani and Bambini, 2014; Friederici and Gierhan, 2013) and may also carry attentional information (Umarova et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous study.

claim: Human EmC connects ventral frontal cortex and insula to the TPJ.
source: Umarova and colleagues found that human EmC connects ventral frontal cortex and insula to the TPJ, namely the core nodes of the human exogenous attention network (Corbetta et al., 2008; Corbetta and Shulman, 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Vertical connections between the dorsal and ventral attention areas provide a structural substrate for attentional integration.
source: Alternatively, vertical connections between the dorsal and ventral attention areas as described here, provide a structural substrate for attentional integration that capitalizes on the full functional repertoire of both streams.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the connectivity data and functional considerations.

claim: Vertical connectivity may be a general theme, a second organizing principle of the visual system in humans and macaques.
source: This vertical connectivity may thus be a general theme, a second organizing principle of the visual system in humans (Kay and Yeatman, 2017; Pestilli et al., 2014) and macaques (Nelissen et al., 2011), extending from attention to other functions requiring vertical integration like language (Cloutman, 2013) or skilled grasping (van Polanen and Davare, 2015).
evidence: This claim is speculative, based on the current findings and citations to related studies.

claim: The work advances the understanding of the architecture of attentional control by suggesting a three-node cortical network, with nodes in three different cortical lobes as the structural substrate of this cognitive function.
source: Taken together, our work advances the understanding of the architecture of attentional control by suggesting a three-node cortical network, with nodes in three different cortical lobes as the structural substrate of this cognitive function.
evidence: This claim summarizes the main contribution of the study.

claim: The description of direct structural connections between attention nodes allows investigations of the 'effective connectivity' between attention areas and the causal impact of these interactions.
source: The description of direct structural connections between these nodes we provide here, now allows investigations of the 'effective connectivity' between attention areas and the causal impact of these interactions.
evidence: This claim is speculative about future research possibilities enabled by the current findings.

claim: Monkeys were cued to pay attention to one of two random dots surfaces to detect and discriminate the occurrence of a coherent motion event.
source: Monkeys were cued to pay attention to one of two random dots surfaces both to detect and discriminate the occurrence of a coherent motion event (see Material and methods).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental task used in the study.

claim: Attentional activation was defined by contrasting blocks with two spatial attention conditions: attend contralateral and attend ipsilateral.
source: To isolate cortical areas modulated specifically by endogenous attention and define LIP and PITd, we contrasted blocks with two spatial attention conditions: attend contralateral and attend ipsilateral (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 1, and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This claim describes the method used to functionally define attention areas.

claim: FEF was defined by means of a guided saccade task where monkeys were required to either maintain fixation or make saccades.
source: FEF was defined by means of a guided saccade task where monkeys were required, in different blocks, to either maintain fixation on a central target, or make saccades (Figure 1B, see also Stemmann and Freiwald, 2016).
evidence: This claim describes the method used to functionally define FEF.

claim: The tract was identifiable from PDD maps in multiple slices between the two ROIs.
source: The tract was identifiable from PDD maps in multiple slices between the two ROIs (Figure 2C) and consistently in all subjects (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by diffusion MRI data shown in multiple figures.

claim: The tract connecting PITd and LIP was consistently identifiable in all subjects.
source: The tract was identifiable from PDD maps in multiple slices between the two ROIs (Figure 2C) and consistently in all subjects (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by diffusion MRI data across multiple subjects.

claim: Ex-vivo data acquisition eliminates experimental confounds and artifacts such as motion, noise, cardiac pulsation, and EPI distortion.
source: We acquired data ex-vivo to eliminate experimental confounds and artifacts such as motion, noise, cardiac pulsation, and EPI distortion.
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge about advantages of ex-vivo imaging.

claim: High angular and spatial resolution dMRI reduces the inherent coarseness of dMRI tractography.
source: We acquired high angular and spatial resolution dMRI, which –along with our relatively small ROIs - reduced the inherent coarseness of dMRI tractography (Thomas et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge and citation to previous methodological work.

claim: Probabilistic CSD tractography improves the robustness of the tractography results, especially to crossing fibers.
source: We used probabilistic CSD tractography (MRtrix 0.2 - RRID:SCR_006971 (Tournier et al., 2012), see below) to improve the robustness of the tractography results, especially to crossing fibers (Tournier et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge and citation to previous methodological work.

claim: Ensemble tractography improves anatomical accuracy and reduces variations in the extent and strength of derived pathways.
source: We used ensemble tractography, that is a combination of candidate streamlines obtained by systematically varying tracking parameters (Takemura et al., 2016a; see also below) to be able to describe tracts that differ in length and curvature, to improve anatomical accuracy, and to reduce variations in the extent and strength of derived pathways, shown to be dependent upon parameters of the tractography algorithm (Jones, 2010; Thomas et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on established knowledge and citations to previous methodological work.

claim: A model-based approach using LiFE removes most false positive tracts.
source: As a final step, we used a model-based approach to the selection of fibers which removes most false positive tracts (Pestilli et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is based on citation to previous methodological work.

claim: Brains were extracted and immersed for 24 hr in 4% paraformaldehyde fixation solution with 0.1% Gd-DTPA.
source: The brains were extracted and immersed for 24 hr in the same fixation solution. Gadolinium- diethylenetriamine penta-acetic acid (Gd-DTPA) (Magnevist, Berlex Laboratories) was added at 0.1% vol to the fixation solution.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental procedure used in the study.

claim: After fixation, the brain was soaked for 5–9 weeks at 4°C in PBS mixed with 0.1% Gd-DTPA to reduce the longitudinal relaxation time (T1).
source: After a 24 hr fixation, the brain was soaked for 5–9 weeks at 4°C in phosphate-buffered Saline (PBS) mixed with 0.1% Gd-DTPA to reduce the longitudinal relaxation time (T1) (D'Arceuil et al., 2007; Wedeen et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental procedure and is supported by citations to previous methodological work.

claim: Diffusion data were acquired with a 3D spin-echo diffusion-weighted EPI sequence with b-value set at 4,025 s/mm2.
source: In brief, diffusion data were acquired with a 3D spin-echo diffusion-weighted EPI sequence. b-value was set at 4,025 s/mm2 (Thomas et al., 2014), which has been demonstrated to be sufficient to model multiple fiber populations in ex vivo specimens (Dyrby et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim describes the experimental parameters and is supported by citations to previous methodological work.

claim: The 3D image matrix size was 320 × 320 × 256, resulting in a near-isotropic spatial resolution of 250 × 250 × 254 μm.
source: The 3D image matrix size was 320 × 320 × 256, resulting in a near-isotropic spatial resolution of 250 × 250 × 254 μm.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental parameters used in the study.

claim: The entire DWI acquisition took approximately 74 hours.
source: The entire DWI acquisition took ∼74 hr.
evidence: This claim describes the experimental procedure.
